is_anopheles.evidence: Study evaluated Anopheles gambiae field populations from Ladji and Malanville in Benin (Page 2, Material and Methods).

reports_target_markers.evidence: Reported kdr (Vgsc L995F/L1014F) mutation frequency in Anopheles gambiae (Page 5, Biochemical Assays and kdr Genotyping, Table 6).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 6 (page 7) reports kdr allele frequency (F[kdr] = 83% at Ladji, n=45; F[kdr] = 6% at Malanville, n=45).

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from field sites in Benin (Ladji, near Cotonou, and Malanville in northern Benin) as larvae and reared to adults (Page 2-3).

is_primary_study.evidence: Primary empirical field trial evaluating experimental huts, bioassays, biochemical activity, and kdr marker frequency.

sub_country_location.evidence: Field collections were conducted in Ladji (Cotonou) and Malanville, Benin (Page 2).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Field collections and trials took place from April to November 2005 (Page 2, Sleepers and Mosquito Collections).

duplicate_risk.evidence: Original primary field study conducted in 2005 at Ladji and Malanville, Benin.

supplement.evidence: All relevant genotype frequency data and sample sizes are fully presented in Table 6 of the main text.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated the efficacy of lambdacyhalothrin ITNs and IRS against pyrethroid-resistant Anopheles gambiae in Ladji (southern Benin) and pyrethroid-susceptible An. gambiae in Malanville (northern Benin). Genotyping confirmed high kdr (Vgsc L995F) frequency at Ladji (83%, n=45) and low frequency at Malanville (6%, n=45).
